mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES remains near its current depressed level while TRANSIT stays flat, weekday foot traffic will not recover and RETAIL_REC will drift lower over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if commuting rebounds without a rise in workplace mobility.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is around -35.6 and TRANSIT around -30.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain within 5 points of current levels for the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in GROCERY_PHARM below its current level signals shorter errand trips and tighter neighborhood-only activity, which will pull RETAIL_REC down within two weeks. The effect fails if grocery mobility rebounds while retail still weakens.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from -10.4 to -12.9 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within the next 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM drops by more than 2 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both increase together, discretionary time shifts toward local outdoor and home-based activity rather than shopping, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if parks rise without a concurrent residential increase.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is persistently positive around 8 to 9 points while PARKS is near baseline to moderately negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both stay above their 4-week average.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT crosses above its recent four-week mean, access to dense commercial corridors improves and retail visits rise within one week. The claim fails if transit improves but retail remains below its prior four-week average.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above its 4-week mean after being below it for at least 2 weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has been stable near -30 for four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher within 7 days after TRANSIT moves above its own 4-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM deteriorates while PARKS remains weak, residents concentrate on essential trips and skip discretionary shopping, causing RETAIL_REC to fall over a four-week horizon. The mechanism fails if grocery weakens but park mobility rebounds strongly at the same time.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS is negative in three of four weeks and GROCERY_PHARM is below baseline throughout
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days despite simultaneous weakness in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained uptick in PARKS is an early signal of weather-supported outdoor substitution, which reduces mall and street retail visits one to two weeks later. The hypothesis fails if park use rises but retail also rises.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by at least 3 points from the prior week and stays above -5
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -7.3 to -9.6 after being -2.7 and -10.1 in prior weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower within 14 days after PARKS increases by at least 3 points and remains above -5.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both recover simultaneously from their current troughs, office-linked lunch and after-work spending will lift RETAIL_REC over four weeks. The claim fails if only one of the two series improves or if retail remains flat.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -33 and TRANSIT rises above -28 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series are currently near their low, with WORKPLACES about -35.6 and TRANSIT about -30.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean within 28 days after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT cross the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in RESIDENTIAL indicates more time spent at home, which displaces discretionary shopping and keeps RETAIL_REC below the last four-week average over the next month. The mechanism fails if residential time stays elevated but retail rebounds anyway.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is positive every week and rose to 9.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean while RESIDENTIAL remains at or above 8 for the next 28 days.
